core_obligations: Inequality (proof lines 3441-3447): for a one-dimensional reduced Nagata local k-algebra with separably closed residue field, the delta-invariant is at least the branch count minus one, branches being geometric branches over the separably closed residue.

Equality analysis (proof lines 3448-3466): passing to the completion preserves branches and delta; the completed ring is strictly henselian; the sharp form of the inequality makes it a wedge of complete discrete valuation rings, each isomorphic to k[[t]] by the coefficient-field lemma, which is exactly the multicross normal form of equation-multicross.
proof_roadmap: State the inequality over the separably closed residue field.
Replace A by its completion, checking invariance of both invariants.
Recognize the strictly henselian property of the completed ring.
Apply the sharp inequality to obtain the wedge of DVRs and normalize each factor to k[[t]].
difficulty_reason: The lemma bounds the delta-invariant by the branch count and classifies the equality case as the completed multicross ring (statement lines 3431-3439). The proof (lines 3441-3466) is complete: the geometric-branches identification, the general inequality, the completion reduction with invariance, the strict henselianness, the wedge-of-DVRs conclusion from the sharp inequality, and the k[[t]] normalization of each branch. Every step is present with no omissions. H2: a systematic chain of local-algebra inputs with correctly ordered hinges.
